atc.skills: clear spoken instructions, spatial reasoning, and accurate decisions from changing information
atc.project: Use a teacher-supervised, non-operational traffic simulation to practice concise directions and tracking movement.
atc.note: School courses are foundations, not ATC certification or specialized radar training. Math choices depend on completed work and placement.

flight.skills: spatial reasoning, physics, navigation, and precise communication
flight.project: Compare maps, weather information and time-distance calculations in a classroom flight-planning exercise.
flight.note: School coursework is not flight training or a pilot qualification.

aviation_operations.skills: accurate scheduling, information management, and clear communication
aviation_operations.project: Plan a fictional transport schedule and explain how changes affect timing and coordination.

air_defense.skills: interpreting technical displays, spatial reasoning, and electronics
air_defense.project: Build a classroom exercise comparing moving objects on a coordinate grid; explain your decisions clearly.
air_defense.note: These are school-level technical foundations, not instruction in weapons operation.

electronics.skills: circuits, measurement, systematic fault finding, and technical documentation
electronics.project: With a teacher, troubleshoot a low-voltage classroom circuit and document the measurements and solution.
electronics.note: At BHS, introductory power and later advanced power courses provide some transferable electrical skills; they are not a dedicated avionics, radar, or medical-equipment repair qualification.

mechanical.skills: mechanical systems, tool safety, measurement, and diagnostics
mechanical.project: Document a supervised mechanical inspection, the evidence for a fault, and a safe repair plan.

aircraft_mechanical.skills: mechanical systems, forces, precision measurement, and maintenance documentation
aircraft_mechanical.project: Use a teacher-approved model mechanism to explain force transfer and how a technician would inspect it.
aircraft_mechanical.note: Automotive or power courses teach transferable mechanical basics; neither school course is aircraft maintenance certification.

fabrication.skills: materials, technical drawings, precision measurement, and fabrication
fabrication.project: Create a dimensioned drawing and a supervised model, then compare the result with the specification.

construction.skills: building plans, measurement, safe construction, and materials
construction.project: Draw a small model structure, estimate materials, and check dimensions with a teacher.

engineering.skills: mathematical modeling, design, technical drawings, and physical systems
engineering.project: Design and test a small classroom structure; document constraints, calculations and improvements.

geospatial.skills: map interpretation, spatial measurement, computing, and geographic analysis
geospatial.project: Compare public maps and measurements and explain uncertainty in a simple mapping project.

electrical_power.skills: electrical systems, energy, measurement, and safe troubleshooting
electrical_power.project: Create a teacher-supervised low-voltage circuit diagram and measure how changing a component changes the circuit.

plumbing.skills: fluid systems, measurement, building plans, and tool safety
plumbing.project: Draw and measure a model pipe layout, explaining flow and access for maintenance.
plumbing.note: These courses support a later plumbing or utilities training route; they do not constitute a plumbing apprenticeship.

transport.skills: route planning, time-distance calculations, safe systems, and logistics
transport.project: Plan a fictional delivery route, calculate timing and explain how delays would change the plan.

logistics.skills: inventory accuracy, scheduling, data handling, and resource planning
logistics.project: Build a small inventory spreadsheet and reconcile a delivery with the original order.

finance.skills: accounting, numerical accuracy, budgeting, and clear reporting
finance.project: Prepare a fictional budget, reconcile transactions and explain a discrepancy.

administration.skills: records accuracy, organization, communication, and people management
administration.project: Create an anonymous fictional scheduling or records project and check it for accuracy.

health_administration.skills: health-system organization, records accuracy, and communication
health_administration.project: Map a fictional patient appointment process using no real patient information.

law.skills: evidence-based arguments, legal reasoning, reading, and writing
law.project: Compare two arguments in a classroom mock case and explain the evidence for each.

policing.skills: law, ethical judgment, communication, and understanding behavior
policing.project: Discuss a teacher-approved ethical scenario, distinguishing evidence from assumptions.

emergency.skills: hazard awareness, physical science, communication, and emergency readiness
emergency.project: Compare public emergency plans and prepare a classroom safety communication exercise.

cbrn.skills: chemistry, biological systems, measurement, and environmental safety
bhs: Environmental Science B: Human Impacts on Earth’s Systems
cbrn.project: Analyze a teacher-provided environmental dataset using safe classroom methods only.
cbrn.note: Study scientific foundations and safety; no hazardous agents or operational procedures are involved.

cyber.skills: programming, computing systems, logical reasoning, and responsible technology use
cyber.project: Use an authorized classroom computing exercise to document a problem and explain a responsible solution.

signals.skills: electronic communication, technical measurement, computing, and analysis
signals.project: Study signals using a teacher-approved circuit or public dataset, then explain patterns and uncertainty.

intelligence.skills: source evaluation, pattern analysis, geography, and concise reporting
intelligence.project: Compare several public sources on a neutral topic and write a report separating facts from uncertainty.

language.skills: careful listening, language learning, cultural understanding, and accurate interpretation
language.project: Compare translations of a short public text and discuss how culture and context change its meaning.
language.note: Choose a language and the next level appropriate to your experience, not all listed options. A school language is preparation for language learning, not a guarantee of an Army language assignment.

community.skills: cultural understanding, communication, social systems, and evidence-based analysis
community.project: Research a community need using public information, then present an ethical, evidence-based communication plan.

media.skills: visual communication, writing, design, and accurate storytelling
media.project: Create a factual photo essay or short school-approved news story and verify each claim.

music.skills: musicianship, listening, notation, ensemble performance, and practice
music.project: Ask a music teacher to help choose an instrument or voice pathway and prepare a short performance recording.
music.note: Instrument choice and prior experience matter. Beginner courses and advanced ensembles are alternatives, not a checklist; Army performance auditions have separate standards.

culinary.skills: food preparation, sanitation, measurement, and teamwork
culinary.project: Plan a simple menu, scaled ingredients and a food-safety checklist with a qualified teacher.
culinary.note: GHS recommendations here are supporting science and business options; the reviewed catalog does not list a dedicated culinary course.

nutrition.skills: biology, chemistry, nutrition, food preparation, and communication
nutrition.project: Compare a fictional menu with a public nutrition resource and explain the reasoning without giving anyone medical advice.

life_science.skills: biology, chemistry, laboratory accuracy, and scientific data analysis
life_science.project: Analyze a teacher-provided biological dataset and write a lab-style explanation with limitations.

chemistry_lab.skills: chemistry, laboratory measurement, quality control, and data analysis
chemistry_lab.project: Use a safe teacher-supervised measurement exercise to compare repeated results and report uncertainty.

environment.skills: ecology, chemistry, water quality, and environmental measurement
bhs: Environmental Science B: Human Impacts on Earth’s Systems
environment.project: Investigate a public water-quality dataset and explain what the measurements can and cannot show.

clinical.skills: human biology, chemistry, anatomy, patient communication, and careful observation
clinical.project: Interview an approved health professional about the work and education needed for this exact occupation.
clinical.note: High-school science builds a foundation. Clinical professions differ substantially in degree, licensing and Army entry requirements; verify the selected role individually.

nursing.skills: human biology, anatomy, patient care, observation, and communication
nursing.project: Ask an approved nurse about patient care, teamwork and the education route for the selected nursing role.
nursing.note: CNA is an exploration option, not a substitute for nursing education or advanced-practice qualifications.

animal.skills: animal biology, chemistry, observation, and laboratory reasoning
animal.project: Ask about supervised animal-care observation and keep a factual observation journal.
animal.note: Human anatomy courses are not veterinary training. Animal-care, laboratory and veterinary officer roles have different entry requirements.

dental.skills: biology, chemistry, anatomy, precision, and patient communication
dental.project: Ask an approved dental professional about the distinction between support, hygienist and dentist roles.
dental.note: These are shared school foundations, not a claim that dentists and dental support specialists require the same professional training.

behavioral.skills: human behavior, biology, research evidence, and supportive communication
behavioral.project: Review a public psychology study and distinguish findings, limitations and personal opinions.
behavioral.note: School psychology courses do not qualify a student to diagnose or provide therapy.

rehabilitation.skills: anatomy, movement, human behavior, and supportive communication
rehabilitation.project: Ask an approved therapist about rehabilitation goals and observe only where permission and privacy allow.

optical.skills: optics, precision measurement, materials, and visual attention
optical.project: Investigate lenses with a teacher-approved classroom optics experiment and record precise measurements.
optical.note: Optical fabrication is different from optometry or ophthalmology; later specialist training remains necessary.

pastoral.skills: listening, cultural understanding, ethics, and supportive communication
pastoral.project: Practice respectful listening in a supervised community-service activity.
pastoral.note: Chaplain and religious-affairs support roles have distinct education and eligibility routes; high-school courses are only preparation.

field.skills: teamwork, communication, physical readiness, navigation, and responsible judgment
field.project: Plan a supervised team challenge and reflect on communication, preparation and responsibility.
field.note: No school course guarantees military eligibility or selection.

rigging.skills: precision inspection, measurement, materials, and procedural accuracy
rigging.project: Use a teacher-approved model to practice following a specification and documenting quality checks.
rigging.note: School projects do not qualify anyone to inspect or prepare safety-critical parachute equipment.

radiological.skills: human biology, radiation physics, chemistry, and measurement
radiological.project: Use a public imaging or radiation-safety educational resource to explain how measurement supports healthcare.
radiological.note: School science does not authorize use of radiation equipment; clinical, research and technical roles require different later qualifications.

pharmacy.skills: chemistry, biology, accurate calculations, and medication terminology
pharmacy.project: Practice units and accuracy using a teacher-provided non-medical dataset; ask a pharmacist about the profession.
pharmacy.note: Pharmacy specialists and pharmacists have different professional education and licensing requirements. Do not use school exercises to advise on medicines.

hearing_vision.skills: human biology, sensory systems, physics, and patient communication
hearing_vision.project: Explore sound or light in a supervised science activity and ask a professional how it connects to hearing or vision care.

diving.skills: physical readiness, pressure, buoyancy, measurement, and teamwork
diving.project: Model buoyancy in a classroom experiment and explain the forces involved.
diving.note: School fitness or science courses do not qualify anyone for diving; specialist supervision and training are essential.

utilities.skills: mechanical systems, electricity, fluid systems, and fault finding
utilities.project: Draw a simple energy-flow diagram for heating or cooling and discuss safe inspection methods with a teacher.

mortuary.skills: biology, careful records, respectful communication, and human behavior
mortuary.project: Ask about a respectful informational interview focused on professional responsibilities and education.

animal_handling.skills: animal behavior, biological observation, responsible care, and communication
animal_handling.project: Ask about an approved animal-care observation opportunity; do not attempt specialist dog training independently.

food_safety.skills: biology, chemistry, sanitation, measurement, and accurate inspection records
food_safety.project: Compare public food-safety guidance with a fictional inspection checklist in a supervised class.

fire_support.skills: spatial reasoning, numerical accuracy, physics, and precise communication
fire_support.project: Practice coordinates and time-distance reasoning using a non-operational classroom simulation.
fire_support.note: These are academic foundations, not weapons instruction.

construction_equipment.skills: mechanical systems, measurement, earthwork planning, and safe equipment use
construction_equipment.project: Use a model site plan to compare dimensions, materials and how equipment access affects the work.
construction_equipment.note: School mechanical and drafting work provides preparation; specialist equipment operation requires separate training.
